policy_note: Default policy is 90% line coverage per source file. After the larql-compute-metal extraction (ADR-019), this crate is CPU-side only — the trait, the CpuBackend impl, pipeline types, and env-option helpers. Every file is expected to clear the 90% floor without `exclude_globs` hacks. GPU-shader coverage lives in `crates/larql-compute-metal/coverage-policy.json`. 2026-06-06: the two inherited debt baselines (`attention/decode.rs` 55%, `kv_dispatch/cpu.rs` 88%) were retired — `attention/decode.rs` is now 92.3% and `kv_dispatch/cpu.rs` 97.1%. The q4k-direct decode path is driven directly via the `Q4kFixtureIndex` fixture (`run_attention_block_decode_step_q4k_direct`, no env var needed) plus an env-gated `attention_step` test (LARQL_Q4K_DIRECT_ATTN, OnceLock-owned by that single test). Residual misses in decode.rs are attention-bias / QK-norm / v-norm branches absent from the gemma3/tinymodel Q4K fixtures (no fixture carries attn biases); residual misses in cpu.rs are the indirect-matvec `coarse_decode_step{,_with_state}` arms, which need an index that supports cached-decode but NOT direct-matvec (structurally hard — both consume the same Q4_K slices). 2026-07-22 (DEC prep): the large-file splits (pipeline/, kv_dispatch/, attention/decode/, cpu/ops/{moe/expert,q4_common,q4k_q8k_dot}/) re-home those documented residual misses into dedicated files, where they no longer average against well-covered siblings: attention/decode/dispatch.rs carries the attention-bias/v-norm/multiplier branches (no fixture arch carries attn biases), kv_dispatch/cpu/dispatch.rs the structurally-hard indirect-matvec coarse arms, attention/decode/q4k_direct.rs scattered failure branches whose tests live in larql-kv. Baselines below are local --package lower bounds (CI's cross-crate measurement reads higher); raise toward 90 and retire when a bias-carrying fixture arch exists. 2026-07-23: CI moved to rust 1.97 whose coverage instrumentation shifts line attribution; the x86 CI profile (no aarch64-gated tests) measured three files under 90 after the DEC-prep merge: cached.rs 89.88 (the 1.97 clippy question-mark rewrite deleted covered lines), ffn/weight.rs 86.21 (FormatRoute dispatch shrank the file), tensors.rs 61.46 (untouched on this branch - pre-existing x86-profile gap newly surfaced). Baselines set just under measured; raise toward 90. 2026-07-31: ffn/expert_weight/trace.rs baselined at 76 - the summary-JSON metric unions the lib-test and integration-binary instantiations of the crate, so lines only reachable from one instantiation (the private open_sink/record_into failure arms, unit-tested; the OnceLock env sink, driven end-to-end by tests/test_moe_route_trace_{on,off}.rs one-test binaries) count uncovered in the other. Merged lcov for the same profdata reads 85%+. Retire if the metric ever de-duplicates instantiations. 2026-08-13 q6k.rs baseline 67%: the uncovered block is `q6k_sb_sum1_asm`, the hand-asm Q6_K kernel from PR #207 (3.47x on aarch64). It still decodes the PRE-FIX interleaved nibble layout while the scalar reference is now ggml-planar, so `q6k_matvec_asm_matches_scalar_bit_exact` is #[ignore]d and the dispatcher routes every arch past it. This is quarantined known-wrong code, not untested code — executing it to raise the number would assert nothing about a kernel that computes the wrong thing. Clear the baseline by reworking the asm to planar and un-ignoring that test, or by deleting the kernel; do not clear it with tests that only call it. 2026-08-14: `kquant_forward/cached.rs` was split into `cached/{timings,predict,fused,native}.rs` for the per-file size budget. Its 89.0 debt baseline moved to `cached/native.rs`, which is where the untested code actually was — the other three pieces come out at 92.8-100% and are now held to the full 90.0 default, so the split tightened this crate's policy rather than relaxing it. `native.rs`'s residue is scattered defensive branches in the native attention/FFN decode steps (missing-tensor and shape-mismatch early returns); clear the baseline when a synthetic fixture drives those refusals.
